title: A locally Noetherian decent algebraic space is quasi-separated
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian: every scheme admitting a representable etale map to $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Assume $X$ is decent: for every field $L$ [def-weil-field] and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$, its pullback over every affine scheme mapping to $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Then $X$ is quasi-separated: the absolute diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Equivalently, for every pair of affine schemes $U,V$ with representable etale maps to $X$, the scheme $U\times_X V$ is quasi-compact. No quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0BB6 (lemma-locally-Noetherian-decent-quasi-separated). Decency is written explicitly as quasi-compactness of field-spectrum maps, as in the existing locally-separated-space-decent node.

proof.text: Fix affine etale scheme charts $U\to X$ and $V\to X$, and put $W=U\times_XV$ and $p:W\to U$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], $W$ is a scheme and $p$ is etale, since it is a scheme test of $V\to X$. Hence $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points]. The map $j:W\to V\times_{\mathbf Z}U$ is a monomorphism: a section is a pair of sections of $V,U$ with equal images in the sheaf of sets $X$, so the pair determines it. The structure map $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ has affine source, hence is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Apply [lem-a1-space-monic-diagonal-tests] with its $X=V$, $Y=W$, $T=S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and $B=U$, using the monomorphism $j$. Its closed-diagonal conclusion says precisely that $p$ is separated. Thus all four hypotheses needed for the fibre-degree lemmas hold without any quasi-separatedness assumption on our original space $X$.

source.place: Tag 0BB6, first paragraph; separatedness required by Tags 086R and 07RY made explicit via scheme-test diagonals.

proof.text: For each $u\in U$, compose $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ with $U\to X$. Decency, in exactly the field-map formulation of the item, says that $V\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is quasi-compact, since $V$ is affine. This is $W_u$ by the universal property of the fibre product: both specify a $V$-section with prescribed image in $X$. It is etale over $\kappa(u)$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], it is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $\kappa(u)$. These open components cover a quasi-compact space, so only finitely many occur. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] their union is the spectrum of their finite product of fields. This product is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(u)$-algebra, so $W_u$ is finite with a well-defined nonnegative degree $\delta(u)$. This includes the empty fibre, whose algebra is zero and degree is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BB6, finite-fibre argument, using directly the field-map definition of decency instead of choosing monomorphic residue representatives; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL.

proof.text: The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and locally Noetherian by the hypothesis on $X$, so it is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] its irreducible components are finite in number. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] each has a generic point $\eta_i$. Put $n=\max_i\delta(\eta_i)$, taking $n=0$ when $U$ is empty. The new lemma [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-lqf-degree-superlevel-open] makes $D=\{u:\delta(u)\ge n+1\}$ open. It is empty: if it met a component at $u$, its intersection with that component would be a nonempty open and would contain its generic point (the closure of that point is the component), contradicting the choice of $n$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], every point lies in an irreducible component; thus $\delta(u)\le n$ for all $u$. This produces a uniform bound from finite generic degrees, rather than assuming quasi-compactness of $W$.

source.place: Tag 0BB6, generic-degree maximum and emptiness of U_{n+1}; more-morphisms.tex Tag 086R.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-lqf-bounded-stratification] to $p:W\to U$: step 1 supplies flatness, local finite presentation, separatedness and local quasi-finiteness, and steps 2 and 3 supply finite fibres with degree bounded by $n$. It gives closed subsets $\varnothing=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Z_n=U$ and disjoint locally closed strata $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ covering $U$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to give each $Z_r$ its reduced induced closed-subscheme structure and $S_r$ its open-subscheme structure inside $Z_r$. Applying the cited universal property to the morphism $S_r\to U$ shows that $W_r=W\times_US_r\to S_r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ for every $0\le r\le n$. Empty strata and degree zero are permitted.

Each $S_r$ is quasi-compact. Here is the topological argument, so no finiteness theorem about subschemes is being suppressed. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], closed subsets of the Noetherian scheme $U$ satisfy the minimal condition. Equivalently, every nonempty family of open subsets has a maximal member. For any subset $A\subseteq U$ and any cover $A\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in I}O_i$ by ambient opens, take a maximal finite union among $\{\bigcup_{i\in J}O_i:J\subseteq I\text{ finite}\}$. Adjoining any $O_i$ cannot enlarge it, so this finite union contains all the $O_i$ and covers $A$. Thus every subspace $A$ is quasi-compact, in particular $S_r$ with its locally closed subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 0BB6 final paragraph expanded using the minimal condition for Noetherian spaces; properties.tex lemma-Noetherian-topology.

proof.text: The map $W_r\to S_r$ is finite by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], hence affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Cover the quasi-compact scheme $S_r$ by finitely many affine opens, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The inverse image of each is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2), hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. These finitely many inverse images cover $W_r$; any open cover of $W_r$ therefore has a finite subcover, by taking finite subcovers on the finitely many inverse images. Thus $W_r$ is quasi-compact. This argument also handles $S_r=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0BB6, final paragraph, finite-locally-free strata are quasi-compact; affine-cover proof spelled out.

proof.text: The projections $W_r\to W$ are continuous and their images cover $W$. Indeed, let $w\in W$; since the $S_r$ partition $U$, the point $u=p(w)$ lies in some $S_r$, and we write $s$ for the corresponding point of the scheme $S_r$, lying over $u$. The ring $\kappa(w)\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(s)$ is a tensor product of two field extensions of $\kappa(u)$, hence nonzero and has a prime ideal; by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] there is a point of $W_r=W\times_US_r$ mapping to $w$. Pull any open cover of $W$ back to each quasi-compact $W_r$, choose a finite subcover there, and combine these for $0\le r\le n$. The resulting finite set of opens covers $W$. Hence $U\times_XV$ is quasi-compact for every pair of affine etale charts. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-affine-pairs-test-quasiseparated] to obtain quasi-compactness on scheme tests of $\Delta_X$, as required. We use a finite partition by locally closed images, not an isomorphism of $W$ with their scheme coproduct. No global quasi-compactness of $X$ was used.
